messages:
Evan Brooks: Quick ask for @eng-runtime — marketing is finalizing the webinar slides + a launch blog. We need validated benchmark numbers and reproducible artifacts for three models so we can lock copy and a small comparison table.

Evan Brooks: Models we want measured: redwood-3b-gguf, redwood-7b-q4, redwood-13b-fp16. Seq lengths: 512 and 2048. Load profiles: single-request (concurrency=1) to show latency and concurrent burst (concurrency=12) to show throughput.

Evan Brooks: Required outputs from eng: a single consolidated CSV, raw per-request logs, exact commands and container tags used, sample input files for each seq_len, and one representative output per model we can paste in the blog. Also note any flaky runs or retries you see.

Lina Gomez: We can do this. Couple clarifying points: 1) report model-side tokens/s (before tokenization overhead) or end-to-end? 2) for cost do you want our internal hosted estimate or a normalized FLOP/op estimate?

Evan Brooks: Model-side tokens/s is what we need. For cost include both: hosted estimate (use staging/dev pricing table) and normalized GPU-op metric so PMs can compare infra.

Andre Wu: Plan: I'll run the 512 sweep this afternoon and the 2048 sweep tomorrow morning. I will record seed, warmup steps, and kernel selection logs. Will push artifacts to bench-reports and drop a link. ETA consolidated CSV by EOD tomorrow.

Andre Wu: Commands I'm going to use (will paste exact envs in the README):

```
# low-latency single-stream
docker run --rm -e MODEL=redwood-7b-q4 ghcr.io/redwood/bench-runner:v2 \
  ./run_bench --model $MODEL --concurrency 1 --seq 512 --iterations 60 --seed 1234 --warmup 8 --out /out/$MODEL-512.json
# burst profile
docker run --rm -e MODEL=redwood-7b-q4 ghcr.io/redwood/bench-runner:v2 \
  ./run_bench --model $MODEL --concurrency 12 --seq 2048 --batch 4 --iterations 30 --seed 1234 --warmup 8 --out /out/$MODEL-2048.json
```

Andre Wu: Notes: we'll pin CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES and set MPS_DISABLED=1 for host consistency. We'll also log the selected kernel names (bench has --dump-kernels).

Lina Gomez: Heads up: 2048 runs frequently pick different attention kernels and that can spike p99. We'll include median/p90/p99 and show sample outlier traces. Recommend including a short note in blog about variability for long-context workloads.

Rob Chen: For the blog blurbs we need one plain-English line per model (e.g., "3B gguf: sub-50ms median p50 at seq=512; great for low-latency chat"). Lina/Andre can you write 1-line takeaways and a 1-sentence caveat about variability?

Andre Wu: Will add takeaways to the README. Also adding CSV columns: model, seq, concurrency, p50_ms, p90_ms, p99_ms, tokens_per_s, cost_per_1M_hosted, gpu_op_norm.

Evan Brooks: Also can you run a tiny demo payload we can use in the live webinar (must finish < 60s). Keep the payload simple and deterministic if possible.

Andre Wu: Suggested minimal payload for demo:

```
{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Explain the three main uses of caching in modern web apps in 4 bullets."}], "max_output_tokens": 150}
```

Andre Wu: Expected trimmed output example: "- Reason 1
- Reason 2
- Reason 3
- Reason 4"

bench-bot: started run 61422 for redwood-7b-q4 seq=512 (owner: andre.wu). Report: https://bench.internal/reports/61422

Andre Wu: Pushed the 512 artifacts: https://bench.internal/reports/61422 — includes per-request traces, kernel dumps, and a preliminary CSV. Starting 2048 run now, will report back when it's finished.

Lina Gomez: If 2048 p99 is out of acceptable range, we'll surface options: reduce batch, pin kernel, or recommend a q5 variant for better p99. We'll document tradeoffs.

Rob Chen: If you want copy help for the one-liners or the blog table, I can draft a few options to match our tone. Ping me and I'll jump in. :memo:

Andre Wu: Thanks — I'll upload final consolidated CSV + README with commands and takeaways once 2048 completes (should be by tomorrow EOD).

Evan Brooks: Great — we'll freeze slide copy after that. Appreciate the quick turnaround!
